summary: The app's own sketch solver no longer reports freedom as unknown for sketches whose rank is clear but whose rank factor looks ill conditioned, such as a two-link arm stretched nearly straight, and no longer calls rank clear on an estimate that can miss a weak direction. Rank is clear only when the independent rows are shown to have a smallest singular value of at least 1e-7. Before, that value was estimated by four inverse iterations over the factor's pivot columns. An estimate approaches from above, so a weak direction it nearly missed could be called clear and the sketch's freedom and short-decimal rounding applied; leaving out the columns without pivots also made a nearly straight arm's rank falsely unclear, since its second link leaves a tiny lead in the joint's columns. Now a lower bound over the pivot columns, one over the Frobenius norm of the inverse of their triangle, decides first: it is at most the square root of the rank below the true value, and leaving out columns can only lower the rows' own value, so a bound reaching 1e-7 shows rank clear. Otherwise the singular values of the independent rows themselves are computed: those of S in the transposed factorization R^T = Q S, built by the same rotations as the witness fit within the group's fill limit, and taken densely, accurate to about epsilon absolutely, for groups of at most 32 independent rows; rank is clear when the smallest reaches 1e-7. Larger groups, or a factor that would pass the fill limit, leave rank unclear. The same rule, within the group's fill limit, decides which rows are set aside before a group's first solve. The dense step costs up to about 41 million counted entries of the 400 million work allowance for 30 rows. The bound costs little for a few hundred rows but grows with the square of the rank where the triangle's inverse is dense: in native release builds, solving 3,200 chained midpoints took about 35 ms instead of 7.5 ms and a 2,000-step staircase about 66 ms instead of 22 ms, while a 200-step staircase stayed at about 2 ms. Sketches at a real tangency still solve with freedom unknown, and drags onto one still stop short of it.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. Some sketches that showed freedom as unknown now show their freedom, and a sketch whose rank only an estimate called clear now shows freedom as unknown and keeps its values unrounded. Very large single groups diagnose more slowly. No protocol change.

checklist.schema: No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, CAD, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation or input-version behavior change. WebMCP tools keep their arguments and result fields.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change and no new application controls.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: The Rust arm test now requires every one of its 47 frames, from the start and chained, and the ordinary solve after each, to be diagnosed with freedom 2; three frames from the start and three chained were uncertain before. The tangency drags for radii 10, 100 and 1000 still end limited, the sketches they leave still solve with rank uncertain, a repeated distance beside a near tangency is still redundant, and a weakly held direction is still uncertain. Three rows whose singular values are about 1.7, 1.2e-7 and 1e-8, built so that an inverse iteration from a fixed start nearly misses the weakest direction, stay uncertain. Three nearly parallel rows whose leads all pass 1e-10, and whose smallest singular value is about 9e-9 while an inverse iteration from a fixed start estimates 1.2e-7, also stay uncertain; this failed before. Thirty rows with tiny pivot leads but well-conditioned entries elsewhere, sharing one column, are clear of dependence with no fill limit, at under 60 million counted entries, and unclear when their transposed factor would pass a fill limit of 100. The runtime arm test requires freedom 2 on every frame. All Rust suites, the sketch-solver and benchmark Vitest suites, and the full test suite pass.

publicNotes.summary: Fewer sketches show their freedom as unknown.
changes: Shows the remaining freedom of sketches such as a nearly straight arm, which the app's own solver reported as unknown.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
